study_type_evidence.quote: Female NMRI mice (8–9 weeks, 25–35 g) were injected intraperitoneally (10 mL/kg) with peptides dissolved in sterile PBS

Peritoneal lavage (1.5–2 mL) were collected from three euthanized female CD-1 mice (14 weeks, 32–33 g) after injecting sterile PBS intraperitoneal (4 mL). Peptides were incubated with aliquots (95 μL) of fresh lavage

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: female outbred NMRI; pharmacokinetics 8–9 weeks, 25–35 g; toxicity 24–32 g, ~7 weeks; efficacy 24–27.1 g, 6 weeks (high dose) and 26.8–30.3 g, 7 weeks (low dose)
in_vivo_species.quote: Female outbred NMRI mice (Janvier Labs, Saint Berthevin Cedex, France) were housed in an individually ventilated cage system

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: female outbred CD-1, 7 weeks, 20–23 g (intravenous PK); 14 weeks, 32–33 g (lavage donors)
in_vivo_species.quote: Female CD-1 mice (20–23 g weight, 7 weeks) were injected intravenously (10 mL/kg) in the tail vein with peptides (0.5 g/L) dissolved in sterile saline

ex_vivo_detail: Mouse peritoneal lavage stability: peptides (75 μg/mL) incubated in fresh PBS lavage from three female CD-1 mice at 37 °C for 0, 30 and 60 min, protein-precipitated with TCA and analysed by RP-HPLC at 214 nm (Api137 half-life ~20 min; Api88 >60% intact at 1 h; Onc72/Onc112 >89% intact at 1 h). Also ex vivo recovery experiments in which untreated mouse blood and organ homogenization buffer were spiked with Api88 or Api137.

agents.name: Api88
agents.sequence: gu-ONNRPVYIPRPRPPHPRL with C-terminal amide (O = ornithine; gu = N,N,N′,N′-tetramethylguanidino)
agents.sequence_source: Introduction: 'Apidaecin-derived analogs Api88 and Api137 possess the same sequence, i.e., gu-ONNRPVYIPRPRPPHPRL (O: ornithine, gu: N,N,N′,N′-tetramethylguanidino), and differ only by the C-terminal amide and acid groups, respectively.'
agents.group_n: n = 7 per time point for intraperitoneal PK; n = 4 per time point per peptide for intravenous PK in Methods (Fig. 2 caption states n = 5); n = 5 for organ homogenates; n = 3–7 for urine; n = 7 per dose group in the infection model
agents.group_n_quote: After 10, 20, 30, 60, or 90 min animals (n = 7) were euthanized by carbon dioxide inhalation and terminal bleeding via cardiac puncture.
agents.dose: 5 and 20 mg/kg body weight for intraperitoneal pharmacokinetics (injected amounts 137 and 618 μg); 5 mg/kg intravenously; 2.5 and 1.25 mg/kg intraperitoneally three times post-infection in the efficacy model
agents.route: intraperitoneal (10 mL/kg in sterile PBS) and intravenous (tail vein, 10 mL/kg in sterile saline)
agents.dose_route_quote: injected intraperitoneally (10 mL/kg) with peptides dissolved in sterile PBS ... at concentrations of 0.5 or 2 g/L corresponding to doses of 5 or 20 mg/kg body weight
agents.cmax: 0.6 μg/mL (i.p. 5 mg/kg) and 4.1 μg/mL (i.p. 20 mg/kg); c0 1.0 and 6.2 μg/mL respectively
agents.tmax: not reported (first plasma sampling time was 10 min after i.p. injection, at which the maximum was observed)
agents.pk_quote: the elimination half-life time of Api137 (t½ = 33.8 min) was almost two-fold longer than for Api88 (t½ = 17.3 min) ... the elimination half-life times decreased to 11 and 17 min

agents.name: Api137
agents.sequence: gu-ONNRPVYIPRPRPPHPRL with free C-terminal acid (O = ornithine; gu = N,N,N′,N′-tetramethylguanidino)
agents.sequence_source: Introduction: 'Api88 and Api137 possess the same sequence, i.e., gu-ONNRPVYIPRPRPPHPRL (O: ornithine, gu: N,N,N′,N′-tetramethylguanidino), and differ only by the C-terminal amide and acid groups, respectively.'
agents.group_n: n = 7 per time point for intraperitoneal PK; n = 4 per time point per peptide for intravenous PK in Methods (Fig. 2 caption states n = 5); n = 5 for organ homogenates; n = 3–7 for urine; n = 7 per dose group in the infection and toxicity models
agents.group_n_quote: Apidaecin Api137 ... was administered intraperitoneal (0.3 mL) in seven mice per group three times post-infection (1, 4, and 8 h) as antibacterial therapy.
agents.dose: 5 and 20 mg/kg body weight for intraperitoneal pharmacokinetics (injected amounts 145 and 602 μg); 5 mg/kg intravenously; 2.5, 1.25, 0.6 and 0.3 mg/kg intraperitoneally in the efficacy model; 20, 40, 80 and 120 mg/kg four times daily in the acute toxicity study
agents.route: intraperitoneal (10 mL/kg in sterile PBS) and intravenous (tail vein, 10 mL/kg in sterile saline)
agents.dose_route_quote: The acute toxicity of Api137 was studied by administering doses of 20, 40, 80, and 120 mg/kg intraperitoneally (i.p.) four times daily (0, 3, 7, and 24 h) into female NMRI mice
agents.cmax: 0.2 μg/mL (i.p. 5 mg/kg) and 3.6 μg/mL (i.p. 20 mg/kg); c0 0.22 and 7.8 μg/mL respectively
agents.tmax: not reported (first plasma sampling time was 10 min after i.p. injection, at which the maximum was observed)
agents.pk_quote: the elimination half-life time of Api137 (t½ = 33.8 min) was almost two-fold longer than for Api88 (t½ = 17.3 min), which could be explained by the higher serum stability of Api137

concentration_time_figure.locator: Fig. 2A (i.v. plasma); Fig. 3A,B (i.p. plasma); Fig. 4 (kidney and liver homogenates); Fig. 5 (urine); Fig. 7 (peritoneal lavage % remaining)
concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Pharmacokinetics of Api88 (A) and Api137 (B) and metabolites 1–17 and 1–16 (C,D) after intraperitoneal administration at doses of 5 mg/kg BW and 20 mg/kg BW. Peptides were quantified ... in plasma samples collected at 10, 20, 30, 60, and 90 min post-injection (n = 7).
concentration_time_figure.note: Fig. 2A plots plasma concentration versus time after a single 5 mg/kg i.v. dose (5, 10, 20, 40, 60 min); Fig. 3A,B plot plasma concentration versus time after 5 and 20 mg/kg i.p. doses (10, 20, 30, 60, 90 min); Fig. 4 and Fig. 5 plot kidney/liver homogenate and urine concentrations versus time. Fig. 7 is an ex vivo peritoneal-lavage stability plot of % peptide remaining versus time (0, 30, 60 min).

bioanalytical_method: RP-HPLC (Alliance 2695) coupled online to ESI-QqLIT-MS (4000 QTRAP with TurboV ion-spray source) in positive multiple reaction monitoring mode, quantified against isotope-labelled peptide standards (LOQ 19–59 ng/mL); metabolite identification by nanoACQUITY UPLC coupled to ESI-LTQ Orbitrap XL MS; peritoneal lavage stability by RP-HPLC with UV absorbance at 214 nm
bioanalytical_quote: an Alliance® 2695 HPLC system was coupled online to an ESI-QqLIT-MS (4,000 QTRAP®) equipped with a TurboV™ ion-spray source and operated in positive ion MRM mode
notes: All PK parameters were taken from Table 1 and the Results body. Table 1 reports single mean values without error terms, calculated with PKSolver 'using the concentrations for the terminal elimination phase determined by the software'. Half-lives are route- and dose-dependent: i.p. 5 mg/kg gives 17.3 min (Api88) and 33.8 min (Api137); i.p. 20 mg/kg gives 11.1 min and 16.9 min. No half-life was calculated for the intravenous route; after i.v. 5 mg/kg, plasma levels fell to around the LOQ by 10 min (Api88 1 μg/mL and Api137 0.4 μg/mL at 5 min). No Tmax is tabulated; maxima coincided with the earliest sampling times. Group-size discrepancy: Methods state n = 4 per time point per peptide for the i.v. CD-1 study while the Fig. 2 caption states n = 5; Fig. 4 states n = 5 organs while the i.p. Methods state n = 7. The frequently quoted in vitro mouse serum half-lives (~5 min for Api88, ~6 h for Api137, ~3 h for Onc72, >8 h for Onc112) appear in the Introduction and Discussion but are explicitly attributed to earlier publications (Berthold et al.; Czihal et al.; Knappe et al.) and were not measured in this study, so no in vitro study type is recorded. Likewise the MIC values (~4 μg/mL against E. coli ATCC 25922) and ribosome Kd values are cited from prior work. Onc72 and Onc112 were tested here only ex vivo in peritoneal lavage; their in vivo efficacy data are cited from Schmidt et al.
